To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the spin adduct of PBN with trichloromethane (CCl3).
the spin adducts of phenyl tertbutyl nitrone (PBN) and its deuterated analogs with trichloromethly radical (CCl3) were isolated and positively identified in vitro and in situ.
the trichlorocarbon radical adduct of PBN has been identified as the 2-tert-butyl-2-trichloromethyldiphenyl nitroxide radical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the spin adducts formed in vitro and in the liver of CCl4-treated rats.
the use of PBN and PBD as spin trapping reagents to study the trichloro methyl radical in biological systems.
the identification and quantitation of the trichlomethyl radical adducts of PBN in rat livers exposed in vitro to CCl4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trichloroethyl radical is the reactive metabolite responsible for the PBN-tri-chloroethyl spin adduct.
the spin adduct formed from PBN and CCl4 is the tert-butyl nirtone radical adduct of trichloromethylene.

the PBN-triCl adduct is a phenyl tert-butylethyltrichloromethyl nitrone, i.e. the tert-butyl radical is attached to the nitrogen of the nitrone, and the trichloro methyl radical is attached to a terminal carbon of the tert-butyl chain, i.e. a 1,1,1,2-trichloro-2-(phenyl tert-butyl)-ethyl-1-nitroxide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have positively identified the trichloroethyl radical adduct to PBN as the major spin adduct in CCl4 exposed liver tissue, and that the trichlorocarbonyl radical adduct to the PBN radical is a minor spin adduct in the same system.
the PBN-CCl3 radical spin adduct is formed in vitro and in the rat liver following CCl4 exposure.

the PBN-tri-chloromethyl adduct has been identified in vitro, and that the adducts from CCl4 treated rat livers are most likely the PBN-tricbomethyl adducts, but the adducts are not the only product formed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin adduct of PBN with trichloromethane is formed in vitro and in rat liver in vivo after treatment with carbon tetrachloride.

the mass spectra of the PBN adducts of trichloromethide are consistent with the structure of the trichoromethyl radical adduc of PBN, which is consistent with the structure that we have proposed for the spin adduct of PBN with trichoromethide.
mass spectrometry is an important tool in the analysis of spin adduction products and that deuterated spin traps can greatly enhance mass spectral analysis.
